Artificial intelligence/machine learning round trip positioning method

event-title.$: ENTRY INTO FORCE OF REQUEST FOR SUBSTANTIVE EXAMINATION

section.content: Systems, methods, apparatus, and computer program products for artificial intelligence/machine learning round-trip positioning. A method may include a UE transmitting at least one positioning capability of the UE to an LMF, the positioning capability indicating at least one artificial intelligence/machine learning positioning function, and receiving at least one configuration from the LMF to perform at least one positioning differential measurement based on the at least one positioning capability of the UE. The method may further include the UE performing the at least one positioning differential measurement with at least one network entity according to the received configuration.
用于人工智能/机器学习往返定位的系统、方法、装置和计算机程序产品。一种方法可以包括UE向LMF发送UE的至少一个定位能力，所述定位能力指示至少一个人工智能/机器学习定位功能，以及从LMF接收至少一个配置，以基于UE的所述至少一个定位能力来执行至少一个定位差分测量。该方法还可以包括UE根据接收到的配置与至少一个网络实体执行所述至少一个定位差分测量。

Artificial intelligence/machine learning round trip positioning methodTechnical Field

Some example embodiments may relate generally to mobile or wireless telecommunication systems, such as third generation partnership project (3 GPP) Long Term Evolution (LTE), 5 th generation (5G) Radio Access Technology (RAT), new Radio (NR) access technology, 6 th generation (6G), and/or other communication systems. For example, certain example embodiments may relate to systems and/or methods for Artificial Intelligence (AI)/Machine Learning (ML) round trip positioning.

Background

Examples of mobile or wireless telecommunications systems may include Radio Frequency (RF) 5G RATs, universal Mobile Telecommunications System (UMTS) terrestrial radio access network (UTRAN), LTE evolved UTRAN (E-UTRAN), LTE-Advanced (LTE-a), LTE-a Pro, NR access technologies, and/or MulteFire alliance. The 5G wireless system refers to the Next Generation (NG) wireless system and network architecture. The 5G system is typically built on 5G NR, but a 5G (or NG) network may also be built on E-UTRA radio. NR is expected to support service classes such as enhanced mobile broadband (eMBB), ultra-reliable low-latency communication (URLLC), and large-scale machine-type communication (mMTC). NR is expected to provide extremely broadband, ultra-robust, low latency connections, and large scale networks to support internet of things (IoT). The next generation radio access network (NG-RAN) represents a 5G Radio Access Network (RAN) that can provide radio access for NR, LTE and LTE-a. It is noted that a node providing radio access functionality for a User Equipment (UE) in 5G, e.g. like a node B in UTRAN or an evolved node B (eNB) in LTE, may be referred to as next generation node B (gNB) when built on an NR radio and as next generation eNB (NG-eNB) when built on an E-UTRA radio.

Detailed Description

It will be readily understood that the components of certain example embodiments, as generally described and illustrated in the figures herein, could be arranged and designed in a wide variety of different configurations. Accordingly, the following detailed description of some example embodiments of systems, methods, apparatus, and computer program products for AI/ML round trip positioning is not intended to limit the scope of certain example embodiments, but is representative of selected example embodiments.

3GPP 5G is considering positioning accuracy enhancements for various scenarios, including scenarios with severe non-line-of-sight (NLOS) conditions. A multiple Round Trip Time (RTT) method may help minimize synchronization errors between a UE and a Transmission Reception Point (TRP). Fig. 1 depicts a conventional RTT method in which a Location Management Function (LMF) transmits Positioning Reference Signal (PRS) configuration information to a UE, the information indicating Downlink (DL) PRS configurations associated with different TRPs to the UE. The LMF may also indicate Uplink (UL) PRS information to the UE, on which the UE transmits UL PRS for TRP measurements. The TRP may then transmit DL PRSs and the UE may measure time of arrival (TOA), including synchronization offset and/or propagation delay. The UE may transmit UL Sounding Reference Signals (SRS) in response to DL PRS and the TRP may measure TOA. The base station may then send measurement reports to the LMF, including TRP receive (Rx) -transmit (Tx) time difference measurements. Finally, the LMF may perform subtraction to obtain RTT for each TRP, which may be used to calculate the location of the UE.

Certain example embodiments described herein may have various technical effects to enhance positioning accuracy. For example, certain example embodiments may provide LOS information, such as Rx-Tx time differences, at the UE and the base station prior to acquiring at least one Positioning Differential Measurement (PDM), including whether LOS is detected independently by the UE and the base station, or vice versa, whether an entity is dominant detection, and whether the UE and/or the base station would use AI/ML. Further, various example embodiments may use AI/ML to obtain the most accurate PDM and determine whether cooperation between the UE and TRP is required. Further, certain example embodiments may select the granularity of the PDM and support making LOS information available and obtaining the most accurate PDM. Accordingly, certain example embodiments discussed below relate to improvements in computer-related technology.

Since round-trip (RT) positioning methods require both the UE and the base station to measure the positioning signals and report PDMs, there is a need to coordinate AI/ML usage between the UE and the base station, at least as to how to determine LOS, how to select granularity of measurement, and how to deploy AI/ML (e.g., independently on each side, or jointly on both sides).

To coordinate these determinations, AI/ML RT localization methods may enhance existing RT localization by introducing new elements. For example, a new long term evolution positioning protocol (LPP)/new wireless positioning protocol a (NRPPa) assistance data Information Element (IE) sent from the LMF to the UE/base station may coordinate the deployment and use of AI/ML RT functionality (e.g., RT LOS determination, RT PDM acquisition, etc.). Furthermore, a new Radio Resource Control (RRC) IE or Media Access Control (MAC) Control Element (CE) coordination between the UE and the base station may be provided that may coordinate AI/ML RT procedures and/or use of synchronous AI/ML RT functionality (e.g., whether model switching/deactivation at one end requires action at the other end) at least in terms of LOS determination and PDM granularity selection.

Fig. 2 shows an example of a signaling diagram 200 depicting some example embodiments for implementing AI/ML RT procedures. According to some example embodiments, LMF 220 and NE 240 may be similar to NE 610 and UE 230 may be similar to UE 620, as shown in fig. 6.

In operation 201, the UE 230 may transmit at least one positioning capability of the UE 230, which may indicate at least one AI/ML RT function of the UE 230, to the LMF 220. For example, at least one AI/ML RT function of UE 230 may include LOS determination (e.g., AI/ML-based LOS detector or non AI/ML-based) and/or PDM acquisition (e.g., AI/ML-based PDM or non AI/ML-based, where PDM may include Rx-Tx time difference, carrier phase difference, etc.). However, any other AI/ML RT functionality of UE 230 may be indicated. In various example embodiments, the PDM may refer to any type of PDM associated with, for example, a direct path Rx-Tx time difference, a reflected Rx-Tx time difference (e.g., the strongest N multipaths), and/or an Rx-Tx carrier phase difference.

Similarly, at operation 202, the NE 240 may send at least one location capability of the NE 240 to the LMF 220, which may indicate at least one AI/ML RT function of the NE 240. For example, at least one AI/ML RT function of NE 240 can include an LOS determination (e.g., AI/ML-based LOS detector or non-AI/ML-based) and/or a PDM acquisition (e.g., AI/ML-based PDM or non-AI/ML-based). However, any other AI/ML RT function of NE 240 may be indicated.

Based on the AI/ML RT functionality report received at operations 201 and/or 202, LMF 220 may send configurations to UE 230 and NE 240 to configure AI/ML RT at operations 203 and 204, respectively. In an example embodiment, LMF 220 may send AI/ML RT configurations via LPP and/or NRPPa IE.

For example, the configuration may include UL SRS and DL PRS configurations and may optionally indicate which entity (i.e., UE 230 or NE 240) should transmit first. The configuration may further indicate at least one LOS determination policy. For example, the configuration may indicate whether LOS detection is performed using AI/ML functionality or not, or performed independently by UE 230 or NE 240.

In alternative example embodiments, LMF 220 may select and configure UE 230 or NE 240 to dominate the acquisition of LOS information. The selected entity (i.e., UE 230 or NE 240) may notify the other entity (i.e., UE 230 or NE 240) of LOS information when transmitting its respective RS (i.e., UL SRS or DL PRS), assuming that the UL and DL channels have the same LOS probability due to channel reciprocity. For example, LOS information may be explicitly notified by attaching a LOS flag after RS transmission by a selected entity, or implicitly notified by selecting an RS Identifier (ID) associated with the LOS flag. For example, if UE 230 performs acquisition of LOS information, UE 230 may transmit an LOS flag with the UL SRS and/or select an SRS whose ID is associated with the LOS flag.

In some example embodiments, the configuration may indicate at least one AI/ML-based PDM acquisition policy. For example, LMF 220 may configure UE 230 and/or NE 240 as to whether PDM acquisition is performed using AI/ML functionality, and whether UE 230 or NE 240 uses the respective AI/ML functionality (if any).

In some example embodiments, the configuration may indicate at least one PDM granularity selection policy. For example, LMF 220 may configure UE 230 and/or NE 240 as to how to select the PDM acquisition granularity, e.g., which entity (i.e., UE 230 or NE 240) may select the granularity, whether the granularity is selected based on handshaking between UE 230 and NE 240, after UE 230 and NE 240 evaluate RT configuration, whether the granularity is fixed and set by NE 240, or whether the granularity is independently selected by UE 230 and NE 240, respectively. An entity that selects or determines granularity (i.e., UE 230 or NE 240) may inform the other entity (i.e., NE 240 or UE 230) of the decision.

In some example embodiments, the configuration may indicate at least one policy for AI/ML function coordination between UE 230 and NE 240. For example, the LMF 220 may configure the UE 230 and/or NE 240 to coordinate AI/ML use and its backup mechanism in the event of AI/ML functionality failure. For example, if UE 230 decides to revert to a legacy method for LOS determination or PDM acquisition, LMF 220 may configure UE 230 as to whether UE 230 should inform NE 240 as to whether UE 230 reverts to the legacy method and/or whether NE 240 should follow the decision, or vice versa. As another example, if UE 230 decides to update a function associated with AI/ML RT (e.g., switch and/or deactivate a model between AI/ML models), LMF 220 may configure UE 230 as to whether UE 230 should inform NE 240 about the switch and/or update, and/or whether NE 240 should mirror the decision of UE 230, and vice versa.

In operation 205, ue 230 and/or NE 240 may apply the configuration received from LMF 220, including the coordination policies as described above.

In operation 206, the ne 240 may transmit at least one DL PRS to the UE 230.

In operation 207, the ue 230 may apply AI/ML RT functionality and may acquire a PDM.

In operation 208, the ue 230 may transmit at least one UL SRS to the NE 240.

At operation 209, if UE 230 is configured to dominate the LOS acquisition, UE 230 may send at least one LOS flag (explicit or implicit) to NE 240.

At operation 210, if UE 230 is configured to select the PDM granularity, UE 230 may send an indication of the PDM granularity to NE 240.

In operation 211, the NE 240 can apply the AI/ML RT function and can obtain the PDM.

At operation 212, UE 230 and/or NE 240 may notify the other party (i.e., NE 240 or UE 230) when the AI/ML RT function changes.

In various example embodiments, if UE 230 and/or NE 240 switch/deactivate the model between models for a given AI/ML RT related function, UE 230 and/or NE 240 may notify another entity in accordance with the configuration of LMF 220. For example, if the AI/ML RT resides at UE 230 and NE 240, the model switch must be agreed upon and synchronized (e.g., the model parts may be active simultaneously). As another example, if the AI/ML RT model resides only on UE 230 or NE 240, the entity using the model can inform the other entity not using the AI/ML model about the handover/deactivation.

In operation 213, the ue 230 may send a PDM report including the PDM to the LMF 220. Similarly, in operation 214, ne 240 may send a PDM report including the PDM to LMF 220.

In operation 214, lmf 220 may determine the location of UE 230 based on the PDM reports received from UE 230 and/or NE 240. For example, using PDM reporting, LMF 220 may obtain distance information between UE 230 and each TRP and then triangulate the location of UE 230.

In some example embodiments, as configured by LMF 220, NE 240 may dominate LOS acquisition, select PDM acquisition granularity, and/or notify UE 230 of such information.

FIG. 6 illustrates an example of a system according to some example embodiments. In an example embodiment, the system may include multiple devices, such as NE 610 and/or UE 620.

NE 610 may be one or more of a base station (e.g., a 3G UMTS NodeB, a 4G LTE evolved NodeB, or a 5G NR next generation NodeB), an LMF, a serving gateway, a server, and/or any other access node or combination thereof.

NE 610 may also include at least one gNB Centralized Unit (CU), which may be associated with at least one gNB Distributed Unit (DU). The at least one gNB-CU and the at least one gNB-DU may communicate via at least one F1 interface, at least one Xn-C interface, and/or via at least one NG interface of a fifth generation core network (5 GC).

The UE 620 may include one or more of a mobile device, such as a mobile phone, a smart phone, a Personal Digital Assistant (PDA), a tablet or portable media player, a digital camera, a pocket video camera, a video game console, a navigation unit (e.g., a Global Positioning System (GPS) device), a desktop or laptop computer, a single location device (e.g., a sensor or smart meter), or any combination thereof. Further, NE 610 and/or UE 620 may be one or more of a national broadband wireless service device (CBSD).

NE 610 and/or UE 620 may include at least one processor, denoted 611 and 621, respectively. The processors 611 and 621 may be implemented by any computing or data processing device, such as a Central Processing Unit (CPU), application Specific Integrated Circuit (ASIC), or similar device. A processor may be implemented as a single controller, or as multiple controllers or processors.

At least one memory may be provided in one or more devices, as shown at 612 and 622. The memory may be fixed or removable. The memory may include computer program instructions or computer code embodied therein. Memories 612 and 622 may independently be any suitable storage device, such as a non-transitory computer-readable medium. The term "non-transitory" as used herein may correspond to limitations of the medium itself (i.e., tangible, not signals), rather than limitations of data storage persistence (e.g., random Access Memory (RAM) versus Read Only Memory (ROM)). A Hard Disk Drive (HDD), random Access Memory (RAM), flash memory, or other suitable memory may be used. The memory may be combined with the processor on a single integrated circuit or may be separate from the processor or processors. Furthermore, the computer program instructions stored in the memory and which may be processed by the processor may be any suitable form of computer program code, for example a compiled or interpreted computer program written in any suitable programming language.

The processors 611 and 621, memories 612 and 622, and any subset thereof may be configured to provide a means for corresponding to the various blocks of fig. 2-5. Although not shown, the device may also include positioning hardware, such as GPS or microelectromechanical system (MEMS) hardware, which may be used to determine the location of the device. Other sensors are also permitted and may be configured to determine position, altitude, speed, direction, etc., such as barometers, compasses, etc.

As shown in fig. 6, transceivers 613 and 623 may be provided and one or more devices may also include at least one antenna, shown as 614 and 624, respectively. A device may have multiple antennas, such as an antenna array configured for multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) communications, or multiple antennas for multiple RATs. Other configurations of these devices may be provided.
